doctrine: Measured savings (12-month utility billing or interval/sub-metered data, ideally weather-normalized) are creditable for underwriting NOI impact; modeled-only savings are provisional and should be haircut or excluded from the money test
Modeled savings are appropriate for origination and screening — deciding which measures to investigate — but not for committing capital or setting rent/NOI expectations

A pre-installation measured baseline is required to ever validate post-installation savings; skipping it means the property can never prove the retrofit worked, which undermines the next capital round

Post-installation measurement (at least one full billing cycle, preferably 12 months, weather-normalized) converts modeled savings to measured savings and should trigger a re-underwrite of the NOI/exit-value case
When measured and modeled savings diverge materially, trust the measured number and investigate the model's assumptions (occupancy, schedule, equipment performance curves) rather than the reverse

NOI and exit value are the money test: a measure that saves energy but does not show up in NOI (e.g. tenant-paid utilities under certain lease structures) needs a separate value-capture mechanism before it's fundable on savings alone
origination_prompts: Is there at least 12 months of utility billing or interval data available to establish a pre-retrofit baseline? If not, this must be collected before the plan proceeds to committed capital.
Does the audit's savings claim state whether it is measured (from actual bills) or modeled (from an engineering estimate)? Flag any claim that doesn't specify.
Who pays the utility bill for the measure's end-use (landlord, tenant, sub-metered)? This determines whether savings flow to NOI directly.
Is there a plan to re-measure post-installation, and on what cadence?
feasibility_checks: Confirm the baseline period doesn't include an anomalous year (major vacancy swing, unusual weather, equipment failure) that would distort the comparison
Weather-normalize baseline and post-install data using degree-days before comparing, especially for HVAC and envelope measures
Verify sub-metering exists if the savings claim depends on isolating one end-use from whole-building billing
Check that the lease structure (gross vs NNN vs tenant-metered) actually routes the claimed savings to ownership's NOI before counting them in the exit-value model
data_requirements: lease structure and utility responsibility by unit/tenant
